svg.text: Regulatory Spectrum Discrete Global Grid System · ISM Band Coverage · ITU Radio Region Face Assignment · Black-and-white edition

Each band adds its own hatching
Score firmly with a stylus or dull knife, then fold
Cut cleanly with scissors or craft knife
Apply PVA or stick glue; press to adjacent face
Each face uses a gnomonic projection centered on its dodecahedron face
center. On a gnomonic projection, all great-circle arcs appear as
straight lines, so country borders that cross a fold edge continue as
straight lines into the adjacent face. Geographic continuity across
all 11 fold edges is verified to within 0.006° of arc (numerical
ATU East · ASMG · CCK (KE) · TCRA (TZ) · TRA (AE)
Print page 1 on US Letter (8.5×11", portrait). Select "Actual size" — do not scale to fit.
Cut along all solid outer edges. A sharp craft knife and steel rule gives the cleanest
Score every dashed fold line firmly with a dull stylus or spent ballpoint, running against a
Fold each face upward (mountain fold) along the scored dashed lines. Crease firmly.
Apply PVA or strong stick glue to the GLUE tabs, which are left unprinted so the glue holds.
Work one tab at a time.
Press each glued tab firmly against the inner face of its matching neighbour. Hold 30
The final seam joins the last free edge. Clamp or tape on the outside while the glue sets.
RSDGGS (Regulatory Spectrum Discrete Global Grid System) encodes device
geographic location as a 1–8 byte index rooted in a spherical
dodecahedron. The low two bits of the face index give the ITU Radio
Region. Index length implies resolution: 1 byte = ITU Region · 2 bytes =
sub-regional bloc · 3 bytes = country-level · 4+ bytes = sub-national.
Devices derive regulatory ISM band rules directly from their cell index
IEEE 802.15.4 MAC layer · CBOR encoded · Rust reference impl
RSDGGS — Regulatory Spectrum Discrete Global Grid System · draft-hanley-rsdggs-00 · Dodecahedron faces aligned to ITU Radio Regions · Gnomonic projection per face
